projects.title: ENI Network
projects.description: ENI is a modular Layer 1 blockchain built for commercial adoption. I joined a team of designers, a PM and developers as a UI/UX designer and frontend developer, and designed and built part of the site's pages, including the mobile versions of several of them.

flow.text: I was in the early team, from the first ideas to the third version of the build, before the project passed to another team. Designers, a PM and developers worked it out together through wireframes and MVPs, and every design decision answered to two things: the client's requirements and the conventions of Web3.

projects.title: ASEAN Labs
projects.description: ASEAN Labs is a Web3 project incubator that helps teams build on ENI across Southeast Asia. I designed and built the site on my own, with custom vector illustrations drawn in Figma, a design system set up in code so every page stays consistent, and motion and micro-interactions throughout.

flow.text: Ideas and references from the Web3 incubator space set the direction: a site that stands apart through quiet micro-interactions and motion. MVPs settled the look before the build, and iteration tuned it after.

story.label: The problem
story.text: Our team lacked a professional landing page to stand out in marketing and on social media. The site also needed to set out what the team offers, how it works with projects, and which projects belong to the ENI ecosystem.

story.label: The idea
story.text: This is the website for my team, a Web3 project incubator. I kept the direction simple: 2D animated vector illustrations in solid colours, with each section structured like an agency website. The sections follow what a visitor needs to know, from the capabilities and the process to the ecosystem.

story.label: How it was built
story.text: Once the team agreed with the design direction, I moved on to development with AI. With the right skill.md files and design instructions, the AI agent executed it well.

story.label: The details
story.text: Some of the vectors are custom made by me in Figma, and the logos were made by our team. A design system set up in code keeps every page consistent, with motion and micro-interactions throughout.

projects.title: Kairma
projects.description: Kairma deploys AI employees inside cross-border operations, keeping brand data local on a sealed, on-premise runtime. I designed and built the site on my own. Its model router section shows live AI model rankings from the OpenRouter API, each part of the platform is an isometric illustration, and the page uses smooth scrolling. I used AI-assisted tools for the imagery.

flow.text: Consultations and MVPs refined the UI/UX and technical decisions. Once the client was satisfied with the MVP, the build went ahead with minimal iteration.

story.label: The problem
story.text: The client wanted a unique landing page for their brand as an AI company, but was unsure how to convey the message about their business. The page had to explain what Kairma does: AI employees for cross-border operations, running on a sealed, on-premise runtime that keeps brand data local.

story.label: The idea
story.text: The client loved the mythical gods in the footer image, so I explored ideas within it and took a myth-inspired direction for the animated illustrations. They are isometric, one for each part of the platform, and the page is structured so that every section uses its space with a clear purpose.

story.label: How it was built
story.text: Consultations and MVPs refined the UI/UX and technical decisions first. AI produced the animated illustrations, guided by specific skill.md files, and the footer image was edited with a dither effect using an open-source website. Once the client was satisfied with the MVP, I moved on to the build with minimal iteration.

projects.title: Stashcube
projects.description: Stashcube is a curated library for AI-native designers and builders: UI libraries, 3D tools, icons, fonts, inspiration and AI skills, in one searchable place. I conceived, designed and built it end to end.

flow.text: A self-initiated project: the concept came first, a moodboard of references shaped the look, and the build followed.

story.label: The problem
story.text: AI-native designers and builders depend on a kit of libraries and templates. I began by keeping mine in Notion, but as the collection grew it needed a better way to sort and categorise it.

story.label: The idea
story.text: Stashcube started as a library of curated libraries for my own use. Most of them are open source, so I decided to share it with the community and the public. It now gathers over 200 links across 15 categories, from UI libraries and 3D tools to icons, fonts, inspiration and AI skills.

story.label: The structure
story.text: Everything is sorted into categories, with a Recently added section for new finds and a My go-to stack section for my own picks.

story.label: The look
story.text: A moodboard of references came first. From it I chose a partial-pixel theme: it has character without overpowering the content, so the libraries stay the focus.

projects.title: FlowFi
projects.description: FlowFi is decentralized infrastructure for the institutional management of on-chain capital, built on ENI. It runs two treasuries: a Governance Treasury that sets the rules and consensus, and an Investor Treasury that grows capital through deployment and incubation. Its FF token launches through the Black Hole Launch, a fair-launch distribution. I designed and built the landing page that sets out the protocol, its tokenomics and its roadmap.

flow.text: The design direction was proposed first, then polished and adjusted to the client's requests.

story.label: The problem
story.text: The client needed a landing page that explains what FlowFi is, along with its tokenomics and roadmap. There is a lot to set out: two treasuries, and a fair-launch token distribution through the Black Hole Launch.

story.label: The idea
story.text: I looked for inspiration that resonates with FlowFi. The on-scroll trigger animation fit best, because its flowing motion blends naturally with the name. I proposed that direction first, then polished it and adjusted it to the client's requests.

story.label: The design
story.text: The isometric illustrations are custom made by me in Figma, and the sections follow a clear structure down the page, so the protocol, its tokenomics and its roadmap each have a place of their own.

projects.title: PayGo
projects.description: PayGo lets APIs and AI agents pay per request through x402 on ENI Mainnet. I designed and built the developer site on my own, put together from components of a UI library, with an interactive protocol walkthrough that explains the payment flow.

flow.text: The client came with the idea and the direction, and I consulted on and refined the UI/UX and technical decisions. Once we agreed on the result, I handed the site over to the client's in-house team to run.

projects.title: OpenCrew
projects.description: OpenCrew is a talent marketplace and growth partner for Web3, AI and new finance projects. People can hire its global crew of executives, advisors, consultants, regional leaders and spokespersons, placed into real roles. Its client stories come from projects we incubated, its photos are real, taken at my own offline events, and its illustrations are custom SVGs drawn in Figma.

flow.text: The black and gold theme was agreed with the team before the build, and the site is still maintained after launch.

story.label: The project
story.text: A side project for talent recruiting in the Web3 space. I built a marketplace-style site where people can hire our services, browse the crew, or join it.

story.label: The look
story.text: I proposed a black and gold theme to feel premium and high class, in line with the senior level of talent on offer, and the team agreed with the direction before the build.

story.label: The proof
story.text: The site shows real experience and on-site activity, with photos taken at my own offline events and client stories from projects we incubated. It also presents a talent pool with professional experiences, for clarity.

projects.title: Fortuna HK
projects.description: Fortuna HK provides cross-border education, wealth management and corporate services. I designed and built the multilingual site on my own, starting by helping the client choose a theme and mood that suit the business. The world clock in the footer was made at the client's request, and the imagery is AI-assisted.

flow.text: The client set the design direction. I suggested and refined what it needed, based on their requirements and the nature of the business.

projects.title: Nikola
projects.description: Nikola coordinates AI governance, protocol structure and capital for projects on ENI. I designed and built the site on my own, after helping the client choose a theme and mood that fit the business. Its effects and shaders come from a UI component library.

flow.text: I set the design direction and the client agreed to it. Their guidelines and documentation made the build straightforward.

projects.title: PUSC
projects.description: PUSC is a DAO-governed stablecoin protocol. The client chose the theme and mood, and I built the site to match, with custom shaders and custom assets. It is a microsite for PayGo.

flow.text: A microsite for PayGo with the same mood and its own variation, so there was little to settle before I built it and handed it over.

events.title: Selangor AI & Semiconductor Summit 2026
events.description: I spoke on the Fire Stage at the Selangor AI & Semiconductor Summit 2026. While the programme centred on chips and infrastructure, my session addressed the human side: preparing everyday Malaysians for this shift. I presented the talent-building work of the MyDAC Malaysia and LEJIEND joint venture, which offers free community learning almost every week, online and in person at Outreach Coffee in Bukit Bintang.

events.title: ENI DeFi Week World Tour
events.description: At the opening stop of the ENI DeFi Week World Tour, I introduced the ENI ecosystem and its vision for DeFi collaboration. Organised by ASEAN Labs, the Changsha event brought that conversation to a mainland Chinese audience, with my presentation delivered in Mandarin and English.

events.title: Web3 + RWA Global Infrastructure Summit
events.description: I represented ENI at the Web3 and RWA Global Digital Infrastructure Summit in Hangzhou, connecting with builders and institutions working on real-world assets. The visit brought the ecosystem into conversations across the summit, from the signing wall to the main hall.

events.title: Monster GameFi Soft Launch
events.description: I hosted the Monster GameFi soft launch under the Bali night sky, welcoming partners from HODL and Kripto 101. As host and keynote presenter, I introduced the play-to-earn vision to the community gathering for launch night.

events.title: Chain of Trust
events.description: At an evening hosted with CCACC and Fableration, I explored trust as a foundation for Web3. A live NOVA demonstration took the audience through contracts, mining mechanics and NFT minting, one step at a time.

events.title: Christmas Crypto Gala
events.description: A year-end conversation about meme markets, PayFi and Malaysia’s digital initiatives. I joined the Christmas Crypto Gala panel to discuss what could drive the next wave of crypto activity with a room full of local community members.

events.title: PayGo × ENI Community Night
events.description: An evening with the PayGo and ENI communities, introducing pay-as-you-go payments on ENI Mainnet to local builders. The session closed with a group photograph of the people bringing those ideas into practice.

events.title: NOVA × MEXC Builders Session
events.description: I presented a walkthrough of offline activations and online campaigns, showing how repeated, consistent community work helps build a Web3 brand that people recognise and trust.

events.title: Blockchain Evolution 2025
events.description: At PPAS Bangi, I spoke with builders and newcomers about crypto, PayFi and GameFi heading into 2025. The community session focused on practical routes to adoption and what those technologies could mean for the local Web3 scene.

apps.title: NARO
apps.description: NARO is an AI-driven on-chain asset launchpad on BNB Smart Chain, created by UXUY and Radar DAO. This is the prototype version, built on BNB Testnet. I built the frontend mobile-first with breakpoints scaling up to desktop, covering the primary views: Swap, Mining, Data, Me and My Team. It connects to testnet wallets, and includes a test data mode for previewing every screen.

flow.text: I mapped out the prototype flows, built the mobile-first interface on BNB Testnet, iterated on the interactions and test states, then handed over the build.

story.label: The starting point
story.text: The original NARO app is already live on BSC. I redesigned it mobile first, with breakpoints scaling up to a desktop version.

story.label: The prototype
story.text: The first version is an MVP and prototype on BNB Testnet, with demo data and test transactions. It covers the primary views of the app: Swap, Mining, Data, Me and My Team. It connects to testnet wallets, and a test data mode lets every screen be previewed.

story.label: The look
story.text: The client's team prepared the theme and brand assets, and I worked with them for the prototype, so the interface stays true to the NARO brand.

story.label: How it was built
story.text: I used AI to execute the code and the BNB Testnet integration. After iterating on the interactions and test states, I handed over the build.
